The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.The following full-/part-time position (38.5/19.5 hours per week)  is to be filled as soon as possible in the Institute for Hygiene and Public Health, Section Global Child Health of the University Hospital Bonn:Scientific coordinator (m/f/d)The Section of Global Child Health was established in November 2025 with the appointment of the Endowed Professorship in Global Child Health. The Section’s remit includes research and teaching in Germany and internationally, as well as clinical practice and the applied, practice-oriented engagement with global health challenges affecting children and adolescents. The professorship is structured as a tandem appointment with a corresponding position at the University of Malawi, based in Lilongwe.You will work in close collaboration with the section head in establishing sound research and communication networks with partners in Malawi and GermanyThe professorship focuses on research in the area of neonatal, child, and adolescent health in “Low and Middle Income Countries” (LMICs), identifies barriers to and solutions for improving global child health, and facilitates the transfer of epidemiological and clinical evidence into health care services with the goal of improving the health status of all children globally.It facilitates institutional, national and international networking and collaboration with universities, academic institutions and key development partners.In addition, it provides academic and health policy advice to national and international governmental as well as non-governmental organizations with regard to global child health.The position is initially limited to three years and remunerated according to TV-L EG 13 (German tax ID is a prerequisite). If you currently live abroad, you should be willing to relocate to Germany temporarily. Subject to interest and feasibility, a temporary increase in the scope of employment through third-party funded resources is envisaged.Tasks:This position offers the opportunity to actively contribute to the development of global strategies for improving children's health and to build and design a completely new international research and education structure.- Strategic coordination and management of international research, education and clinical programmes across the two professorships and the EKFS network- Planning, coordination, and monitoring of cross-institutional activities with academic and non-academic partners- Management of communication channels between institutions, disciplines, and countries, ensuring efficient information flow and alignment of activities- Coordination, and implementation of training materials and structured capacity-building programmes in collaboration with international experts- Planning, organisation, and delivery of international workshops and seminars in online and on-site formats- Preparation of annual progress and impact reports, dissemination of results through conferences and other scientific communication formats- Contribution to the strategic development, coordination, and drafting of third-party funding proposals to expand and sustain programme activitiesRequirements:- A full academic degree at Master’s level or higher in a health-related discipline- A strong interest in global child health and international health systems cooperation- Demonstrated experience in project coordination and research management- Excellent organisational skills and a structured, meticulous approach to work- Proven ability to navigate academic hierarchies and university administrative processes, combined with sensitivity to intercultural contexts- Strong teamwork skills, resilience, and the ability to assert and represent set positions- Full professional proficiency in both German and English, written and spoken Willingness to maintain an appropriate on-site presence at the university in Bonn- Previous extended study, research, or professional experience in a low- or middle-income country would be considered a strong assetWe offer: An interesting and challenging job in a modern research institution with attractive research infrastructures and a cooperative and communicative institute culture. On behalf of KINRADEN, MINDWEISS is seeking a commercially minded and hands-on Finance Director to play a key role in the company’s next phase of international growth. With responsibility for strengthening financial management and developing a scalable finance function, you will have significant influence on strategic decisions and the financial foundation supporting KINRADEN’s ambitious retail expansion.

As Finance Director, you will report directly to the CEO and work closely with the wider management team, acting as a trusted financial and strategic sparring partner. You will take full ownership of the finance function, balancing strategic priorities with operational responsibilities while ensuring that financial insights actively support commercial decisions and future investments.

A central part of your responsibility will be to drive financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and performance management, ensuring reliable financial oversight and clear insights into business performance across the organisation and its growing retail operations. You will support strategic and commercial decision-making through financial analysis, business cases and scenario planning, including evaluating the financial implications of new stores, markets and investments.

Furthermore, you will be responsible for cash flow and liquidity management, financial controls and the preparation of relevant management and Board reporting, ensuring transparency and a clear overview of the company’s financial position.

You will also oversee the ongoing financial operations, including monthly closing, annual accounts, audits, tax, VAT and financial compliance. As KINRADEN continues to expand internationally, you will play a key role in developing scalable financial processes, systems and governance to support increasing business complexity and long-term growth.

Strong financial expertise and commercial understanding

To succeed in this role, you bring solid experience from a senior finance position and strong expertise in financial accounting, controlling, budgeting, forecasting and cash flow management. Your ability to combine financial expertise with commercial understanding enables you to support strategic decisions and evaluate business opportunities.

We expect you to have a relevant academic degree in finance, accounting or economics, ideally complemented by experience from an international business with multiple legal entities. A background in retail, consumer goods or luxury would be an advantage, although specific industry experience is not essential. Furthermore, you are fluent in English, have excellent Microsoft Office skills and are able to communicate financial insights clearly and effectively.

A grounded and collaborative finance leader

On a personal level, you are grounded, confident and approachable, with the professional maturity to build trust through your expertise and sound judgement. You take ownership naturally and work independently, while maintaining a collaborative and down-to-earth approach. To thrive in this role, it is essential that you are comfortable navigating changing priorities and can move seamlessly between strategic discussions and hands-on execution. Furthermore, your flexibility and pragmatic mindset enable you to contribute positively to KINRADEN’s informal and creative culture.

About KINRADEN

Founded in 2014 by Sarah Emilie Müllertz, KINRADEN is a modern luxury brand shaped by influences ranging from Japanese design traditions to Danish architecture. With a deep commitment to sustainability, the brand actively supports two of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals: ensuring fair and dignified employment practices (Goal 8), and advocating for responsible production and consumption (Goal 12).

KINRADEN operates with a flat organizational structure and a work culture built on trust, responsibility, and a welcoming, down-to-earth atmosphere. The company embraces a distinctly Danish way of working—informal, friendly, and rooted in strong relationships. Collaboration is key, fostering a close-knit community where people support one another and value inclusivity.

We place emphasis on your competencies, qualifications, and ambitions, as well as a strong mutual fit between you and the company’s culture and values. **Job Description

**

Senior Data Analyst

Posting Start Date: 9/29/26

Alcântara, PRT, 1300‑001, | Gentofte, DNK, 2820,

**Senior Data Analyst – SAP Reporting & Stakeholder Alignment

**

• Location: Copenhagen, Denmark or Lisbon, Portugal

• Working hours: Full-time

• Work model: Hybrid

• Contract type: Permanent

Are you passionate about turning business questions into meaningful data solutions? Do you enjoy working with stakeholders, solving complex data challenges, and transforming data into insights that drive better decisions? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Senior Data Analyst, you will join the Data & Insights team and report directly to the Head of Data & Insights. In this role, you will act as the bridge between business stakeholders and SAP data, ensuring reporting requirements are clearly defined, translated into actionable data solutions, and delivered with accuracy and impact.

You will work closely with Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Operations, and Data Engineering teams to support data-driven decision-making while improving reporting processes and data quality across the organization. This is a great opportunity to influence business decisions, collaborate across functions, and help shape the future of data and analytics at STG.

**What Your Day Will Look Like

**In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Partner directly with business stakeholders — Finance leadership, Sales/Commercial, Supply Chain/Operations — to understand their reporting and data needs, and translate them into concrete data requirements.

• Work closely with data engineers to scope, request, and validate data pulled from SAP, acting as the translation layer between business language and technical/data specifications.

• Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, validate, and consolidate data for recurring and ad hoc reporting.

• Build and maintain Excel-based models, trackers, and reports that stakeholders rely on for decision-making.

• Consolidate data into stakeholder-ready reporting, and supporting data checks.

• Act as the go-to person for scoping ambiguous stakeholder requests — clarifying what's actually needed, managing expectations, and pushing back constructively when a request isn't well-defined or feasible.

• Identify data quality issues at the source and work with SAP module owners and data engineers to resolve them.

• Document data definitions, sources, and logic so reporting stays consistent and auditable month over month.

• Continuously look for ways to streamline the process rather than repeating manual work each cycle.

**What You'll Bring

**

• 5+ years of experience in a data analyst, business analyst, or similar data-facing role, ideally in a retail or consumer business.

• Strong SQL skills — comfortable writing and troubleshooting complex queries independently.

• Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, data modeling; Power Query is a plus).

• Familiarity with SAP data structures, particularly FI (Finance) and SD (Sales & Distribution).

• Experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), or willingness to learn it, is a plus.

• Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Business, Economics, Finance, Data/Statistics, Engineering, or related).

• Proven experience gathering requirements from business stakeholders and translating them into technical/data specifications.

• Strong stakeholder management skills — able to align multiple stakeholders (including Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, and IT/data engineering) with sometimes competing priorities, and communicate trade-offs clearly.

• Comfortable operating with a degree of ambiguity and turning it into a structured plan.

**Working At STG & What To Expect

**At Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG), we are so much more than what meets the eye. We combine the strength of global brands with the entrepreneurial mindset that allows people to make a real impact. Here you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, collaborate across borders, and help shape what's next.

At STG you'll find more than a role. You'll find opportunities to grow, learn from talented colleagues, and contribute to initiatives that help drive business performance across a global organization.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

**Ready to be part of something bigger?

**Apply now and discover much more.

**Our recruitment process

****Requirements

**Before starting our hiring process, your application will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We assess each application against the key competencies and requirements for the role. If your experience and skills are a good match, you'll be invited to continue through our hiring process, which may include the following steps:

• Final interview with key stakeholders

jobs.description:
Who We Are

For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world's leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,500+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds in general.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated in our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

While striving to deliver client value, we believe it is vital to consider our people and our planet in every business decision we make. Acting responsibly is not optional. It is essential.

Why This Role is Important to Us

We are looking for Software Engineers at middle level to join our engineering team that builds fintech solutions for managing OTC (Over-The-Counter) financial instruments within our asset management platform, SimCorp Dimension and SimCorp One. Our work delivers value in two major areas. First, we implement new features that drive the business forward and shape the future of our platform. Second, we focus on extending and maintaining our established solutions to ensure our clients’ operations remain uninterrupted and always available.

What You Will Be Responsible For

• 
Designing, building, and extending existing solutions and APIs for our OTC asset management product, delivering value to customers incrementally.

• 
Working primarily in C#. Our codebase also includes OCaml and APL therefore prior experience with these languages is a strong plus.

• 
Understanding, refactoring and modernizing our legacy codebase without disrupting the business it supports.

• 
Focusing on the systems as a whole and being able address fundamental changes that improves the quality, performance and user experience.

• 
Collaborating closely with your product owner to refine requirements, clarify business needs, and shape how features get built.

• 
Working as part of a team of skilled engineers — pairing, reviewing code, and sharing ownership of the solution with fellow engineers.

• 
Following good engineering practice: clean code, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
Building, extending and consuming REST APIs.

• 
Communicating clearly with both technical and business stakeholders.

• 
Continuously learning — and helping the team and product grow with you.

Required Skills & Experience

• Interest in creating innovative features for a complex platform, working on areas such as API scalability, automation, performance, and operational resilience - having space to explore, design and influence the final solution.

• Good C# skills. This is the core language for the role; your level of seniority will determine how much ownership and architectural input you're expected to bring.

• Experience with, or genuine interest in, functional programming. Familiarity with OCaml, APL, F#, Standard ML, Scala or Haskell is a real advantage but not required — a willingness to learn is what matters most.

• Experience (or strong interest) in refactoring existing code and working with legacy systems.

• Good collaboration and communication skills, with fluency in English (written and spoken).

• A relevant degree (Computer Science or STEM) with demonstrated hands-on experience in software engineering.

Furthermore, We Value That You Are:

• motivated to work within the financial domain,

• comfortable working closely with a cross-functional team,

• willing to learn and pick up new languages and paradigms as needed,

• able to identify tech debt and help drive incremental improvement,

• a collaborative person willing to share knowledge and learn from your team members.

Our Team and Ways of Working

We deliver solution for large scale financial institutions with billions of dollars in managed assets. Therefore, our work impacts everyday of our customers operations. You will work in a small team of highly skilled engineers on whole SDLC process – from understanding customers' needs, through solutioning and design to coding, testing and maintaining our software. Our hybrid model of working includes two days (minimum) in our Copenhagen office and up to three days working remotely. Codebase includes a mix of C#, OCaml and APL which gives broad opportunities to upskill and drive your career with us. We invest a lot in your understanding of both the technical details of the solution and financial knowledge that will allow you to contribute to building the future of asset management.

Our Benefits

Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. However, at SimCorp, we believe we can offer more. Therefore, in addition to the traditional benefit scheme, we provide an excellent work-life balance: flexible work hours, a hybrid workplace model. On top of that, we have IP innovation sprints, where you have dedicated time per quarter to spend on mastering your skills as well as contributing to the company development. There is never just one route — we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

Next Steps

Please click below to apply. Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your CV in English as soon as possible. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is the right fit, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to help you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks. We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone's experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process, we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

Do you enjoy developing people and creating structure in a busy microbiology environment?

Join Bavarian Nordic as a QC Manager and help your team deliver reliable analyses that support the production and supply of vaccines that protect lives.

**Your team and leadership environment

**The Microbiology area consists of eight laboratory technicians and seven scientists organised across two teams. The area performs analytical testing of raw materials, intermediates, finished products, environmental samples and other manufacturing-related samples. Methods include bioburden, TOC, endotoxin, identification using MALDI-TOF and sterility testing.

The laboratory operates seven days a week during daytime hours because certain analyses are time critical. The teams work in a shift rotation covering weekends and public holidays.

You will join a QC department of approximately 90 employees across six teams. Our Core Leadership Team of Senior Managers works closely with First-Line Managers, the Operational Excellence Partner and a Quality Integrator to develop people and processes and maintain strong quality oversight.

QC is undergoing significant change as we support increased production demands, improve efficiency and reduce lead times. As a first-line manager, you will translate changing priorities into clear direction while maintaining employee engagement, well-being and a strong quality mindset.

**Your Responsibilities

**Lead and develop your team. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback and coach employees in their professional development. Build competencies and a supportive working environment where people feel confident raising concerns and take responsibility for quality.

Ensure reliable daily operations. Maintain an overview of workload, sample flow and operational risks. Coordinate priorities and resources to support time-critical analyses and continuity across the laboratory’s seven-day operation.

Maintain quality and improve processes. Ensure activities comply with cGMP and the Bavarian Nordic Quality Management System. Promote data integrity and inspection readiness and improve processes across the sample lifecycle through accurate documentation and reliable sample flow.

Collaborate across QC and manufacturing. Work closely with stakeholders to align testing priorities with manufacturing needs. Use data and digital tools to improve transparency, address bottlenecks and reduce lead times while maintaining quality.

**Your profile

**You combine an understanding of microbiological quality control with a practical, people-focused leadership approach. You remain clear and approachable when priorities change and can balance timely delivery with compliance and employee well-being.

• A relevant scientific degree and experience from a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or biotechnology environment, preferably within QC microbiology.

• An understanding of microbiological testing and its role in supporting manufacturing and product quality.

• Leadership experience from QC, a laboratory or a similar operational area, is an advantage, together with the ability to coach others and build engagement.

• A solid understanding of cGMP, data integrity and Quality Management Systems, and confidence working with LIMS or other digital laboratory tools.

• A structured approach to prioritization and continuous improvement, with clear communication and strong cross-functional collaboration skills.

**Why join Bavarian Nordic

**You will lead a team whose work supports the quality of vaccines supplied to people around the world. The role offers the opportunity to strengthen daily operations, develop employees and influence how Microbiology collaborates with the wider organisation.

You will be part of a leadership team that values collaboration, coaching and building strong competencies. As QC evolves, you can contribute to continuous improvement, digitalisation and Operational Excellence while developing professionally in an international vaccine company.

**Ready to make a difference? Apply now!

**Apply by clicking the ‘APPLY’ button. We are interviewing on an ongoing basis and look forward to receiving your CV.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

**For us, it is all about improving and saving lives

**Improving and saving lives through innovative vaccines is at the heart of what we do at Bavarian Nordic. We are a fully integrated vaccine company focused on the development, manufacturing and commercialisation of life-saving vaccines, and the largest pure-play vaccine company in the world.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

__Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

_For more information, visit _www.bavarian-nordic.com

Every year, European governments spend billions on mobility: subsidies, contracts, licences, public transport. Most of that money is spent with no clear idea of what it buys for society.

We're building the tech layer that changes that.

What we do

Impact Market builds MIMA, the Mobility Impact Market. On our platform, cities and transport authorities incentivise mobility operators (bike share, e-scooters, car-pooling, car sharing, bike leasing) for trips according to their benefit to society: a car trip replaced, emissions avoided, space and congestion saved, health improved, a neighbourhood connected. By estimating the socio-economic impact of each trip, we design smart incentives that get the most social value out of public funds.

The idea is much bigger than mobility: governments paying for the outcomes they want, with the evidence to back it up. Mobility is our first market, and we intend to move into other areas of public spending.

Where we are

• 
Funded with 12+ months runway

• 
Several paying public-sector clients

• 
A production platform (prod + staging), with live trip and rider-survey data from operators flowing in since August 2026

• 
A team of 3. You'd be number 4.

The role

You'll be our first technical hire and will lead product and engineering. For now that means hands fully dirty: you write the code. No agencies, no outsourcing.

• 
Own the platform. Rust, Postgres, cloud, our RiderSurvey API, and the data pipelines from operators. You'll inherit a working MVP and decide what to keep, what to rebuild and what to build next.

• 
Make the big calls, including the language. We chose Rust deliberately: we think a strict compiler and type system are the right guardrails for building fast with AI. If you have a better argument for something else, convince us.

• 
Be AI-native. We expect you to use AI seriously in coding and every other technical task. That's how a team of four does the work of fifteen.

• 
Build agents that run the company with us, for account management, client reporting and forecasting.

• 
Grow into the science. Together with a future R&D lead, you'll work on the statistical significance of measured impacts and on forecasting how markets respond to incentives.

• 
Shape the product with the founders and our clients. You'll be in the room with transport authorities, not behind a ticket queue.

You

• 
Have minimum 4 years of relevant experience shipping production software, ideally backend or data-heavy systems

• 
Senior and still love writing code every day? Even better.

• 
Know Rust, or are genuinely motivated to go deep in it (not just "willing"). (We are not dogmatic about Rust, but we have a working platform built with care, so changing direction would take strong conviction.)

• 
Already build with AI tools daily and have opinions about how to do it well

• 
Are comfortable with data: SQL, pipelines, and an appetite for statistics and forecasting

• 
Take ownership when things are ambiguous, and like it when nobody tells you how

• 
Care about the mission. You don't need to have read our founder's book, The Next Democracy, but its core ideas about how citizens and governments could work together - is fundamental to what we do. If they don’t excite you, this probably isn't the right fit.

Bonus points for experience in mobility or transport, govtech, causal inference or experimentation, or privacy-by-design and GDPR.

What we offer

• 
A real say in everything. Stack, product, architecture, culture and who we hire next.

• 
Title decided together. We're advertising this as CTO / Founding Engineer and will settle the title with you based on your experience and ambitions.

• 
Competitive startup salary plus a meaningful warrant package, designed to make total compensation comparable with bigger-company offers

5 weeks of holiday and flexible hours

Work that matters. Help redirect public money towards what actually improves people's lives.

Impact Market aims to transform public procurement like Google and Facebook transformed marketing. Impact Market facilitates payments for outputs, and allows public institutions to pay for the projects that create the outcomes they seek. Instead of choosing one service, public authorities can work with multiple companies, and allow them to compete and innovate in creating the results. They can experiment and scale the projects that deliver results. We are focusing on new mobility services as a starting point, allowing cities to pay for innovative mobility services which reduces their use of personal cars.

Read more about Impact Market

About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• 
Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• 
Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• 
Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• 
Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• 
Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• 
Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• 
Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• 
Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• 
A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• 
Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• 
Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• 
Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• 
Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• 
Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• 
Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• 
Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• 
Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like for the Team You'll Join

• 
Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• 
Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• 
Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• 
The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• 
The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• 
A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• 
A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• 
An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

Working at

Photoncycle

Solar panels produce plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that problem: we store this energy next to house, so the household can use it for electricity and heating all winter. Surplus power is sold on the electricity market, where it helps balance supply and demand. The household pays a fixed monthly fee, and we build, install and operate the system. Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems combine solar energy, long-duration storage, and energy trading, so households can use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy for households. We are 25 employees with offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026 we raised a €15 million Series A led by NordicNinja and Voima Ventures. We are now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, and the first phase of our production plant is underway.

jobs.occupation: Hydrographic Surveyor & Systems Technician at HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor
jobs.description:
Would you like to become the technical go-to person for the systems that keep a fleet of working vessels accurate and operational? At HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor, you will take ownership of dredging systems, survey equipment and onboard IT across the fleet, with plenty of freedom to shape how the area is run.

Take technical ownership across the fleet

HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor has delivered marine construction projects since 1958 and today works across Northern Europe within dredging, offshore wind, coastal protection and maritime infrastructure.

As the fleet grows, HØJ wants to bring more technical knowledge in-house. You will join the technical team in Horsens, where you will take specialist responsibility for the systems connecting dredging operations, positioning, survey equipment and onboard IT. While your colleagues cover other technical areas across the fleet, your primary focus will be the dredging systems and the related IT and survey technology.

Your main focus will be the 3D dredging systems across seven vessels, including Teledyne PDS, positioning equipment, sensors and the supporting IT setup. You will work closely with skippers, crews, project managers and suppliers and become the person they turn to when systems need to be set up, improved or brought back online.

Some days, you will work alongside your colleagues in the technical team in Horsens, planning and coordinating maintenance, configuring systems or supporting vessels remotely. Other days, you will be on board troubleshooting equipment, preparing a vessel for a new project or carrying out planned service and maintenance.

The aim is not only to solve problems when they occur, but to create a more consistent, well-documented and reliable setup across the fleet.

More specifically, you will:

• Take technical ownership of the fleet’s dredging systems and Teledyne PDS setup

• Work with positioning, sensors, multibeam and other survey equipment

• Support and improve onboard IT, networks and communication systems

• Plan preventive maintenance, calibrations and service

• Document the technical setup on each vessel and prepare relevant reports

• Support crews and project managers with troubleshooting and project preparation

One of your first tasks will be to map the existing system landscape across the vessels. You will also help commission the dredging system on a new vessel and establish clearer standards across the fleet.

Sådan ansøger du

Læs mere og søg her:

Søg job

Leading the commissioning strategy, team and schedule from mobilisation to integrated systems testing.

**Role Overview

**The Commissioning Manager leads Sensori's commissioning function on a project, ensuring mechanical and electrical systems are started, tested and proven safely, in the right sequence and to the client's acceptance criteria. The role develops the commissioning plan and schedule, manages commissioning engineers and vendor resources, controls the interface with the client's commissioning agent, and integrates commissioning requirements into the construction program so that handover is predictable and fully documented.

**Principal Duties And Responsibilities

**

• Develop and own the project commissioning plan, including strategy, organisation, level definitions, sequences, acceptance criteria and documentation requirements.

• Build and maintain the commissioning schedule; integrate it with the construction program and drive readiness of systems and areas to support it.

• Lead, allocate and develop the team of commissioning engineers; coordinate vendor and subcontractor commissioning resources.

• Chair commissioning coordination meetings with construction, quality, Authorised Persons, vendors and the client's commissioning agent.

• Oversee development and approval of method statements, checklists, test scripts and integrated systems test procedures.

• Manage the energisation and start-up sequence in conjunction with the Senior Authorised Person, ensuring permits, isolations and safety controls are in place.

• Monitor test execution, witness critical tests and ensure results are recorded, reviewed and accepted in the commissioning management system.

• Manage the commissioning issues log; drive closure of deficiencies with construction teams, subcontractors and vendors.

• Plan and lead integrated systems testing, including failure scenarios and redundancy demonstrations, with the client and third parties.

• Ensure complete, accurate turnover packages, training and documentation are delivered for handover.

• Report commissioning progress, risks and constraints to project leadership weekly; contribute to lessons learned and improvement of Sensori's commissioning standards.

• Support pre-construction and tenders with commissioning strategies, durations and resource plans.

**Selection criteria / person specification

**

• Degree in Mechanical, Electrical or Building Services Engineering, or a trade qualification with extensive commissioning leadership experience.

• At least seven years in commissioning, including several years leading commissioning teams on data centre, pharmaceutical or mission-critical projects.

• Strong understanding of both mechanical and electrical systems, sequences of operation and integrated testing.

• Experience working with client commissioning agents and formal level-based commissioning processes.

• Proven ability to plan and schedule commissioning within a construction program and to manage readiness across trades.

• Familiarity with commissioning management software and structured documentation.

• Strong leadership, coordination and communication skills; able to chair meetings and influence senior stakeholders.

• Sound knowledge of safe systems of work for energisation and live testing.

• Willing to travel and to be site-based for extended periods.

Mechanical Engineer – FLOWVISION A/S

About FLOWVISION A/S

FLOWVISION A/S is a Danish engineering company founded in 2006, specialized in designing and delivering advanced emission abatement systems for combustion-based power plants worldwide. Since 2021, the company has been part of AXENS GROUP, while continuing to operate as an independent business with its own organization, commercial responsibility, and market-facing role.

The company operates in an international EPC environment and delivers technically advanced solutions to customers within the energy, oil & gas, and industrial sectors across multiple global markets. FLOWVISION collaborates closely with major international players and is recognized for its strong technical know-how, high-quality standards, and ability to solve complex engineering challenges.

Today, FLOWVISION employs around 20 highly skilled specialists, creating a strong concentration of technical competencies and deep industry expertise. This gives the company the agility and close collaboration of a small expert team, combined with the backing and broader industrial context of being part of Axens.

FLOWVISION offers a flat organizational structure, short decision-making processes, and a collaborative culture where openness, knowledge sharing, and teamwork are essential parts of everyday life.

The company is currently experiencing significant growth and a strong order intake, creating attractive opportunities for professionals who want to influence both project execution and the continued development of the business.

The position

As Mechanical Engineer, you will become part of FLOWVISION’s highly specialized engineering environment and play a key role in the execution of technically advanced international EPC projects.

You will work closely with our Lead Mechanical Engineer, Project Managers, workshops, suppliers, and external engineering partners to ensure that mechanical designs, fabrication documentation, and technical solutions are delivered with high quality and according to demanding project timelines.

The role combines hands-on engineering with close interaction across fabrication, welding, procurement, and project execution activities. You will contribute throughout the entire project lifecycle — from bid clarification and design reviews to fabrication support, inspections, and final documentation.

This is a role for someone who enjoys solving practical engineering challenges, working close to production realities, and operating in an environment where technical quality, collaboration, and execution are critical to success.

You will also have the opportunity to influence engineering processes and contribute to the continued professionalization and growth of the business.

Key responsibilities

Mechanical project execution

• Participate in technical reviews of RFQ packages and specifications during bidding and project execution phases.

• Support clarification processes and ensure alignment of technical scope, assumptions, and interfaces.

• Define mechanical design requirements and coordinate engineering inputs towards external engineering and drafting partners.

• Work with mechanical drawings and technical documentation, including general arrangements, structural steel drawings, piping layouts, isometrics, and fabrication documentation.

• Support structured engineering milestone reviews and contribute to design acceptance and design freeze activities.

• Identify and resolve technical issues, deviations, and design changes throughout the project lifecycle.

• Assess manufacturability and propose practical engineering improvements related to fabrication, welding, installation, and assembly.

Fabrication, welding & workshop interface

• Act as a daily technical interface towards workshops and fabrication partners.

• Handle technical clarifications during fabrication and pre-assembly activities.

• Participate in workshop activities such as PIM, pre-FAT, FAT, inspections, and technical follow-up.

• Support resolution of punch items, deviations, and non-conformities together with Project Management and QHSE.

Documentation & engineering coordination

• Prepare and consolidate mechanical engineering documentation for customer deliveries.

• Work actively with engineering data, revisions, BOM structures, and document control processes.

• Support procurement activities through technical review of supplier quotations and deviations.

• Contribute to maintaining technical quality, traceability, and compliance across all project phases.

Qualifications

We expect you to have:

• A technical degree within Mechanical Engineering or a similar engineering discipline.

• Experience from project-based engineering environments, fabrication, workshops, or EPC project execution.

• Practical exposure to welding, piping, valves, structural steel, or process equipment.

• Strong ability to read, review, and assess mechanical and fabrication drawings.

• Familiarity with relevant standards such as ASME and EN1090.

• Experience working with AutoCAD or similar 2D/3D CAD systems. Plant3D is preferred.

• Experience working with drawings, revisions, BOM structures, and document management systems.

• A structured, analytical, and proactive mindset with strong attention to detail.

• The ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, quality, procurement, and project functions.

• Strong English communication skills, written and spoken. Danish is considered an advantage.

Practical information

• Location: FLOWVISION A/S, Odense, Denmark

• Reporting line: COO / Lead Mechanical Engineer

• Travel activity: Approx. 20–30 days annually depending on projects

What we offer

FLOWVISION offers a unique opportunity to become part of a highly specialized and growing international engineering company where technical know-how and collaboration are the core drivers of success.

We offer:

• A key technical role in an international and rapidly growing engineering company.

• The opportunity to work on technically advanced and highly challenging international EPC projects.

• A unique environment with a strong concentration of specialist competencies and technical expertise.

• Excellent opportunities for professional and personal development as the company continues its growth and professionalization journey.

• A high degree of influence on engineering solutions, project execution, and ways of working.

• A flat organization with fast decision-making and close collaboration across the company.

• A versatile and dynamic workday characterized by openness, cooperation, flexibility, and humor.

• A strong development culture with high ambitions regarding quality, innovation, and employee well-being.

• Office location in Odense with international exposure and limited travel activity.

FLOWVISION is a company where highly skilled people work closely together to deliver complex solutions to global customers — and where the right person will have the opportunity to make a visible impact on both projects and the future development of the business.

Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, and candidates are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.
